"The essential fly-fishing guide to Greater Portland, Oregon From the tidewaters of the Columbia River to a host of other rivers as well as streams, ocean bays, and reservoirs, the wondrous and diverse region around Portland, Oregon offers something for every angler. But how do you know when and where to fish, how to get there, and what kind of gear to use? The answers are all here in Quick Casts: Portland-the most accurate and up-to-date angler's resource available on a place that offers some of the finest sport fishing in the Pacific Northwest. Local angler and author Jim Yuskavitch knows these waters, and here he brings together the information that will help other anglers fish them. Answering the questions every angler asks before setting out, he provides descriptions of fishing hot spots, including top locations. He provides a list of the game fish at each location and the best times to fish; tips on lures, flies, bait, tackle, and techniques; information on access and regulations; and maps and photos. An illustrated section describing the habits, habitats, and the best ways to fish for the region's huge variety of game fish rounds out this essential Portland-area angling companion. "--
"Describes the state's fishing from the tidewaters to the high desert in the east"--

Machine generated contents note: I. IntroductionII. Tips and Advice Basic information on fishing in the greater Portland area, overview of available fish species and habitat preferences along with a discussion of anadromous fish run timing and some general fishing advice relating to the fishing locations highlighted in the book. Also reviewed would be angling license and tag requirements, and some important regulations such as those dealing with wild versus hatchery fish. III. Northwest of Portland1. Multnomah Channel, Willamette River Opportunities for salmon, steelhead, shad, sturgeon, bass, walleye, catfish and perch about 40 minutes from Portland. 2. Gilbert River, Sauvie Island Walleye, catfish, sturgeon and bass 50 minutes from Portland. 3. Smith and Bybee Lakes Located about 15 minutes from downtown Portland, crappie, bullhead, bass, bluegill and perch. 4. Willamette and Columbia Rivers, Kelly Point Park Good angling opportunities for sturgeon, salmon and steelhead at the confluence of the Willamette and Columbia rivers, 25 minutes from Portland. IV. Southwest of Portland5. St. Louis Ponds Rainbow trout and a variety of warmwater fish 50 minutes from Portland. 6. Henry Hagg Lake Trout, bass, crappie and perch. A 60-minute drive from Portland. 7. Pudding River Cutthroat trout, with small stream fishing opportunities in its tributaries. 45 minutes from Portland. 8. Gales Creek A first-rate and accessible winter steelhead and trout stream 45 minutes from Portland. 9. Tualatin River at Cook Park Good opportunities to use a float tube or pontoon boat to catch bass. About 20 minutes from Portland. 10. Willamette River at George Rogers Park Catch a variety of Willamette River warmwater species where Oswego Creek flows into the main river. 20 minutes from Portland. 11. North Fork Yamhill River Nice, small stream angling for native, wild cutthroat trout 45 minutes from Portland. V. Southeast of Portland12. Clackamas River at Carver Park A 30-minute drive from Portland. Fish available, depending upon the time of year, includes Chinook and coho salmon and steelhead, along with rainbow trout. 13. Clackamas River at Milo McIver Park Chinook and coho salmon, steelhead and rainbow trout. It is a 55-minute drive from Portland. 14. Sandy River at Oxbow Park Excellent bank and wading access 50 minutes from Portland to fish for Chinook salmon, coho salmon and steelhead. 15. Sandy River at Sandy Hatchery A 50-minute drive and 30-minute hike to the Sandy River to catch steelhead and Chinook and coho salmon. 16. Eagle Creek at Bonnie Lure Park Another top, easily accessible Chinook and coho salmon and steelhead stream 45 minutes from Portland. 17. Molalla River A spring Chinook and winter steelhead stream 50 minutes from Portland. 18. Clackamette Park, Willamette River Fishing for salmon, steelhead, sturgeon and warmwater species at the junction of the Willamette and Clackamas rivers 25 minutes from Portland. 19. Estacada Lake A reservoir on the Clackamas River 50 minutes from Portland offers fishing for steelhead, trout, and coho and Chinook salmon. 20. Sandy River at Lewis and Clark State Park Fishing for salmon and steelhead where the Clackamas River enters the Columbia River, 25 minutes from Portland. VI. Northeast of Portland Nearby Fishing in Washington State A brief overview of nearby fishing opportunities across the state line including licensing and tag requirements, and other considerations of note to non-resident anglers

metadata.description: Logbook of a whaling voyage to the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. Includes descriptions of whales seen or taken, accidents, a death at sea, punishments, illnesses, interactions with natives, and shipboard medicine. Also contains whale stamps, poetry, listing of personal items, an account of items sold, list of ships, chronometer corrections, list of letters for various ships, and a list of natives hired and discharged. One man died of pleurisy on September 27, 1841. One man was punished for causing a leak in a cask of molasses on October 23, 1841. One man fell from aloft and hurt his leg badly on December 2, 1842. Whaling grounds include the Western Islands, Cornell, Coast of Brazil, Coast of Chile, Callao, On Shore, Galapagos, On the Line, Tuamatos, Archer, and Juan Fernandes grounds.; Old Dartmouth Historical Society (ODHS 1193); Whaling vessel out of New Bedford, Mass., mastered by E. Sun, sea and secrets. A week on the sunny Greek island of Kethos is just what Alice Archer needs, even if she has to put up with her difficult sister. Stella's tantrums are a fair price to pay for crystal-clear waters, blue skies and white clifftop villas. When Alice meets Milo, a handsome gardener at the Villa Argenti, for the first time she suddenly feels beautiful, alluring and confident. But is it just holiday magic or will the irresistible pull between Alice and Milo survive against all odds?

creator: Cicero (Ship)
Chadwick, William J.,--mate
Wrisley, Isaac
metadata.description: Logbook of a whaling voyage to the Atlantic, Pacific, and Arctic Oceans in addition ot the Sea of Okhotsk, the Yellow Sea, and the Sea of Japan. Includes descriptions of whales and walruses seen or taken, illnesses, accidents, deaths at sea, interactions with natives, desertions, a rescue, and punishments. Also contains illustrations of whales, pen and ink drawings of the rigging, a drawing of a clipper ship, profile views, oil shipped home, accounts of provisions, and a crew list. A heavy gale damaged the windlass on September 1, 1861. On 4 September 1861, the vessel took two men from the ship Emily Morgan who had originally belonged to the bark Alice Frazier when lost. One whale caught on 23 March 1862 was eaten by sharks before the crew was able to cut in. A Japanese war steamer took possession of the Bonin Islands on 5 April 1862 but the Cicero encountered no problems. Isaac Wrisley assumed logkeeping duties on 13 November 1862 after William Chadwick (First Mate) was fired for incompetence. One man died of consumption on December 28, 1862. The vessel took on a passenger to Guam in February 1863. The vessel was damaged by ice on July 17, 1863. The keeper reported that the vessel was leaking on October 11, 1863. The vessel was damaged by a typhoon on October 16, 1863. On 4 June 1864, the vessel encountered several starving people on McKean Island (Kiribati) and gave them some supplies. A sperm whale stove a whaleboat on June 14, 1864. The vessel took a passenger off the brig Kohala to the Sandwich Islands in August 1864. One man was sick with rheumatism on October 13, 1864. John Rotch fell overboard on 29 January 1865 but was saved. The Steward died on April 14, 1865. Other places represented include Cape Verde, Marquesas Islands, Maui, Bonin Islands, Honolulu, Saipan, Guam, and Lahaina. Whaling grounds include the Cape Verde, Coast of Brazil, Falkland Islands, Coast of Chile, Tuamotos, Japan, On the Line, Japan Sea, Okhotsk Sea, and the Bering Sea grounds.; Old Dartmouth Historical Society (ODHS 18); Whaling vessel out of New Bedford, Mass., mastered by John R. Stivers, on voyage 9 October 1860 - 25 May 1865; managing agent, Loum Snow; built in Rochester, Mass., 1823.

metadata.description: Mackenzie, Alexander (Sir): 1763-1820. Born on island of Lewis; immigrated to New York then Montreal; entered service of Finlay, Gregory & Co., c. 1779; subsequently employed by Gregory, McLeod & Co. and NWC; in charge of Fort Chipewyan from 1788; retired to England, 1799; created knight bachelor, 1802; returned to Canada and fur trade, 1802-1808; cousin of Roderick Mackenzie (Wallace, Dictionary of Canadian biography ). // Combe, William: 1741-1823. Prolific English writer; assisted Alexander Mackenzie in preparation of Voyages , 1801 ( Dictionary of National Biography ). // Mackenzie, Roderick: d.1844. Fur trader; cousin of Sir Alexander Mackenzie; brother of Henry MacKenzie (Wallace, Dictionary of Canadian biography ). // After the preface there follow 132 pages on the history of the fur trade in the North West. Some authorities think this was written by his cousin, Roderick MacKenzie. According to the Dictionary of National Biography , Voyages , 1801, was compiled by William Combe from Mackenzie's notes. Includes vocabularies of the Knisteneaux, Algonquin, Chepewyan, Nagailer, and Atnah Indian languages. Errors in paging: page ix numbered xi; page 190 unnumbered; pages 212-216 numbered 214-218. Also published, 2nd edition, London: Printed for T. Cadell and W. Davies, 1801 ([2], cxxxii, viii, 412, [2]p.); including some material by Bougainville, London: Printed for T. Cadell, Jun. and W. metadata.description: Logbook of a whaling voyage to the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans and the Okhotsk Sea. Includes descriptions of whales seen or taken, accidents, shipwrecks, and women on ships. Also contains whale stamps and anchor drawings. Crew boarded the abandonded bark Alice Frazier on 22 June 1861 in the Okhotsk Sea. In September 1862, the vessel dragged and just missed the Milo (Ship) in Shantar Bay. In June 1863, the vessel drifted into the ice and remained blocked in the ice for 50 days. Other places represented include Turtle Bay (Baja California, Mexico), Kahawai (Hawaii), Hope Island, Fabius Island and Rocky Point (Siberia), and Fabius Island (Nedorazumeniya Island). Whaling grounds include the San Antonio, Cornell, Coast of Brazil, Cape Horn, On the Line, Coast of Japan, East China Sea, Japan Sea, Okhotsk Sea, and the Coast of Califonria grounds.; Old Dartmouth Historical Society (ODHS 262); Whaling vessel, out of New Bedford, Mass., mastered by Charles Halsey, on voyage 6 September 1860 - 6 Aprril 1865; managing agent: Henry Taber & Company ; built at Milton, Mass., 1815.

metadata.description: Journal of a whaling voyage to the South Pacific and Indian Ocean. Includes descriptions of whales seen or taken, accidents at sea, illnesses, deaths at sea, punishment, and women onboard. Also contains a crew list, provisions, religious verses, and prayers. The ship lost 5 boats in the Indian Ocean as a result of a heavy gale. The crew received word of the murder of two missionaries by natives on February 10, 1840. On February 25, 1840, the steward attacked the captain and was punished. On April 25, 1840, while at Tahiti, one crewman "not being in his right mind" jumped overboard and drowned. The crew list is at the back of the book as well as a list of who raised whales. There are also numerous verses, prayers and references to the Scriptures. After seven months out the ship got its first whale. There were passengers from Oahu to New Bedford, including Reverend Dr. Lafon, his lady, and native servants. Dr. Lafon held church services every Sunday on the voyage home.; Old Dartmouth Historical Society (ODHS 306); Whaling vessel out of New Bedford, Mass., mastered by Abraham Gardner, on voyage 29 June 1839 - 19 March 1893; managing agent, Alexander Gibbs; built in Middletown, Conn., 1815.

Guided by her loving mother and brash father, Peppa is stuck almost every day. Her little siblings, however, look up to Peppa lovingly. 6:15am Blue's Clues & You! Series 3 Episode 4: A Blue's Clues Festival of Lights A special, surprise guest comes to Periwinkle's house to celebrate Chanukah; Josh and Blue play Blue's Clues to figure out who the surprise guest is, and celebrate the holiday by spinning dreidels, frying latkes, and singing. 6:40am Oggy Oggy Series 1 Episode 20: The Garbage Collectors People around town show so little consideration for the rubbish collectors that one of them decides to quit his job. In response, Oggy Oggy offers to help them out in his own imaginative way. 6:45am Odo Series 1 Episode 7: Fowl Play Odo isn't chosen for the camp football team because he's 'too little'. So Odo and the little birds challenge the big birds to a football match. 6:55am Fireman Sam Lost In The Caves Fun with the friendly fireman and the villagers of Pontypandy. 7:05am Thomas & Friends: All Engines Go Series 2 Episode 6: Carly's Magnificent Magnet When Carly gets a new magnet to help Tess the Troublesome Crane load up a shipment of metal crates, she struggles with the new tool. 7:15am Mecha Builders Series 1 : The Treasure Of Treetop Woods Ranger Nat's hike turns to adventure when he finds a treasure map, but he can't read it. Fortunately, the Mechas are ready to lend a hand and help him locate the mysterious treasure. 7:30am Peppa Pig Series 3 Episode 10: Washing Daddy Pig hangs his clean football shirt out to dry, but Peppa, George and Mummy splash it with mud. They put it in the wash, but Peppa puts her red dress in too - which turns Daddy's shirt pink.  7:35am Peppa Pig Series 1 Episode 2: Mr Dinosaur Is Lost George is distraught when he loses Mr Dinosaur, his favourite toy. 7:40am PAW Patrol Series 7 : Pups Save the Maze Explorers Mr. Porter and Alex go on a sightseeing hike but get trapped inside a huge maze! The Paw Patrol has to find the maze and their friends! 8:00am SpongeBob SquarePants Series 5 Episode 3: Friend or Foe 8:30am PAW Patrol Series 6 : Pups Save the Squirrels The Paw Patrol is on a roll when squirrels stash acorns in Alex's treehouse causing it to fall onto Daring Danny's skateboard! 8:40am Kangaroo Beach Series 1 Episode 4: Island Campout Camping out overnight on Boomerang Island with the cadets, Frizzy goes on a late-night hunt for an alien koala. 8:50am Milo Series 1 : Milo The Astronaut Milo is a little cat lucky enough to live with his mum and dad at their dry cleaner. Their robotic washing machine Suds lets Milo and his friends try on different costumes, opening their eyes to a world of possibilities. 9:05am Peppa Pig Series 1 Episode 10: Gardening Peppa and George enjoy helping Grandpa Pig plant seeds in his Garden. 9:10am Milkshake! Story Den Series 2 Episode 5: From Root to Shoot Joining Derek in the Story Den to read `From Root to Shoot', a story that explains that anybody can reach for the stars regardless of who they are or where they might have come from. 9:15am Jeremy Vine Series 6 Episode 85 Jeremy Vine discusses and dissects the latest news, views and opinions with guests. 12:45pm Dogs Behaving (Very) Badly Series 4 Episode 9 Dogs Buzz and Roshi used to be best pals, but after Christy and Scott moved into their new home, all hell broke loose and the brothers went to war. Antique dealer Carlos needs to make a grand per day to support his family. Andy and Sue have spent thousands on a static caravan. 5:00pm 5 News at 5 National and international news. 6:00pm Eggheads Series 23 Episode 60 The Eggheads team are made up of some of Britain's top quizzers. They face a team of challengers trying to beat the incumbents in order to win a cash prize. If the Eggheads beat the challengers, the cash prize is rolled over to subsequent episodes. 6:30pm Eggheads Series 24 Episode 1 Trying to topple the Eggheads today are the Allotment Boys from Essex. This team of green-fingered friends enjoy spending their spare time at the allotment they share in Braintree. 7:00pm Coastal Devon & Cornwall with Michael Portillo Series 1 Episode 3 Michael Portillo travels across the two counties in south-west England. 8:00pm A Country Life for Half the Price Series 5 Episode 1 The presenter meets families who made a leap from town to country. In Shropshire, she visits the Goldby family who traded suburban Epsom for a quiet hamlet. 9:00pm Dalgliesh Series 2 Episode 2: Death of an Expert Witness: Part 2 Enigmatic detective Adam Dalgliesh, a specialist in unusual murders, works to solve a series of intricate and mysterious crimes in 1970s England. 10:00pm 'allo 'allo!: Forty Years of Laughter Meet cast and crew, who share their memories of the show. We hear backstage secrets, and discover the fate of that infamous painting, The Fallen Madonna with the Big Boobies. 11:30pm Paul Merton's Heroes Of Comedy Paul Merton explores what motivated the greatest comics. From Charlie Chaplin, Laurel and Hardy to Victoria Wood and Jo Brand, Paul discovers what drove them to the top. 1:20am Entertainment News On 5 A daily round-up of showbiz news and gossip from around the world, focusing on celebrities, movies, music and entertainment. 1:25am Teleshopping Shopping from home. 3:25am Sinkholes Series 2 Episode 4 Sucking down homes and destroying lives, sinkholes can appear from nowhere and have devastating consequences. Featuring stories from the UK and around the world and the people who have seen their houses destroyed by sinkholes. 4:10am Friends Series 4 Episode 5: The One With Joey's New Girlfriend Chandler falls for Joey's new date, Ross discovers that the woman that he thinks he's dating actually thinks he's the babysitter, Rachel's new college boyfriend steals, and Phoebe tries to re-catch a cold to improve her singing voice. 4:35am Friends Series 4 Episode 7: The One Where Chandler Crosses the Line Chandler finally confesses to his feelings for Kathy just after she splits up with Joey, Ross rediscovers his hopeless musical skills on the keyboard which Phoebe alone appreciates, and Chandler buys new furniture for the apartment since the robbery left them with just the canoe, chick and duck. 4:55am Friends Series 10 Episode 7: The One With the Home Study Monica and Chandler fuss over their apartment as they expect a visit from the adoption worker. Meanwhile, Phoebe and Mike opt for a small wedding and donate the extra money to a children's charity. 5:20am House Doctor Camberley A divorcing couple need to revamp their Victorian semi in Camberley, Surrey. 5:45am Peppa Pig Series 4 Episode 5: Naughty Tortoise Dr Hamster's pet tortoise Tiddles gets stuck up a tree. Who is going to come to the rescue? 5:50am Pip & Posy Series 1 Episode 25: Wizard's Picnic The friends keep telling lies to hide that they secretly ate Frankie's cupcakes.

metadata.description: Log/journal, kept by John Smith Taber, comprised of three whaling voyages. First voyage documents the Ship Condor of New Bedford on a whaling voyage to the Cape Verde, Coast of Brazil, Falklands. Contains entries dated 15 July 1832-27 May 1833. The voyage was conducted on behalf of owner/agent. Second voyage documents the Ship Frances Henrietta of New Bedford on a whaling voyage to the San Antonio, Cape Verde, Coast of Chile. Contains entries dated 15 June 1833-9 September 1834. The voyage was conducted on behalf of owner/agent. Third voyage documents the Ship Isabella of Fairhaven on a whaling voyage to the. Contains entries dated 24 May 1838-30 August 1838. The voyage was conducted on behalf of owner/agent. An account of coastal shipping between Boston and Norfolk, VA; strictly concerned with weather & location.

Autobots Rangers Ms. Mimi sometimes called Thea Stilton (voiced by Larissa Murray to Sarah Edmondson) is the headteacher at Camembert Academy and is the main Protagonist of the series, the brave and valiant leader of the Autobots, in Angelina Ballerina: The Next Steps. Lola Bunny (voiced by Kristen Wiig) is a loyal, courageous, and fun-loving Autobot scout and Bugs Bunny's girlfriend from The Looney Tunes Show. Lola talks a mile-a-minute, can be absent-minded on occasion, super friendly and adorable, and grows on anyone who is around her long enough. Larry (voiced by Brian Drummond) is the Autobots' pragmatic medical officer smarter Lambeosaurus from Dinosaur Train. He and his family are the neighbors of the Pteranodon Family who live in Pteranodon Terrace.  Rex (voiced by John Goodman) is an orange Tyrannosaurs and the main character and the Autobots' scrappy English-accented weapons specialist of the film We're Back! franchise. Milli (voiced by Madeleine Rose Yen) is the first lieutenant of the Autobots and Ms. Mimi's second-in-command who displays a hip-hop-like personality form Team Umizoomi series. Juniper Lee (voiced by Lara Jill Miller) is the Autobots' combat instructor resident of Orchid Bay City, and June is an 11-year old Asian-American girl gifted with magical power that grants her the abilities and title of Te Xuan Ze, the role of protector of the hidden world of magic. Blossom (voiced by Catherine Cavadini) is the Autobot Commander and Leader; she's the bright but egocentric leader of the superhero trio. Buttercup (voiced by Jo Wyatt) is the Autobot Toughest Fighter; she's the bravest, most headstrong of the superhero trio. Jenny Wakeman (voiced by Janice Kawaye) is an Autobot sharpshooter and a state-of-the-art robotic protector of Earth, armed with advanced weaponry and devices at her disposal, but wishes to live the life of a normal teenager.  Dexter (voiced by Candi Milo) is a Autobot boy genius who has a secret laboratory. His intelligence makes him the brains of the family and he is one of the world's greatest inventors, having created countless weird and amazing machines and experiments.  Lapis Lazuli (voiced by Jennifer Paz) is a Seeker and former member of the Crystal Gems. she sacrifices her spark to allow Ms. Mimi to use her components and weaponry to destroy The Pest. Dragon (voiced by Adrian Truss) is a is an Autobot Air-Soldier young member of an airborne herbivore species of dinosaur who evolved over millions of years from carnivorous ground-dragons. He is Jane's best friend and is usually there when she needs him. He is one of the strongest members of the Fire Villains, being Fire Lord's right hand hench-bot, while serving as a secondary/supporting antagonist in Ordeal of Fire.  The Kraang are a mutant decepticon race of brain-shaped aliens from Dimension X, piloting robotic bodies called Kraangdroids that are either covered in a blue bodysuit, or not. Jack-Bots are Mandark's regularly occurring minions in the Xiaolin series. He customized them in different shapes, weapons and forms to better suit his needs or wants. Cerberus: a mutant three headed dog with adds with Sari Sandac's head. Charybdis: a mutant sea monster whose inhalations formed a deadly whirlpool or a huge water mouth. Chimera: a mutant fire-breathing, three-headed monster with one head of a Tyrannosaurus mcraeensis, one of a serpent, and another of a pig, Tyrannosaurus mcraeensis's claws and jaws in front and pig's legs behind, and a longest serpent tail. Gorgons: male and female mutant monsters depicted with serpent on their Dee Dee's head instead of hair, and sometimes described as having tusks, wings, and brazen claws. Lernaean Hydra: a mutant gigantic many-headed, dragon-like creature that guarded an Underworld entrance beneath Lake Lerna.  Manticore or Androphagos: having the body of a indian lion, a Smurfette's face with three rows of sharp teeth sometimes two heads by conjoined twins, and the wings of a bat or dragon. Minotaur: a mutant monster with the head of a cattles and the body of a humans. Orthrus: a two-headed mutant dog. Scylla: once a nereid, transformed by Circe into a mutant many-headed, tentacled monster who fed on passing sailors in the straits between herself and Charybdis by plucking them off the Autobot rangers's ship and eating them. Sirens: mutant bird-like women whose irresistible song lured sailors to their deaths. Cyclopes: three one-eyed giants who forged the lightning bolts of Zeus and Helmet and Bident of Hades. Some assisted the god Hephaestus at his workshops. Children of Gaia and Uranus, who were locked by Uranus in Tartarus. According to Hesiod, their names were Arges, Brontes, and Steropes. Geryon (Γηρυων): according to Hesiod, Geryon was a mutant giant with one body and three heads, whereas the tradition followed by Aeschylus gave him three bodies. A lost description by Stesichorus said that he has six hands and six feet and is winged; there are some mid-sixth-century Chalcidian vases portraying Geryon as winged. Some accounts state that he had six legs as well, while others state that the three bodies were joined to one pair of legs. metadata.description: Log of a merchant ship en route to Honolulu around Cape Horn, the only port of call. This is the log of a non-whaling vessel that travelled from New Bedford around Cape Horn to Honolulu and stayed there for six months. It then returned home after discharging unspecified cargo and coal, cleaning and painting the ship, and taking on board whale oil, some bone, hides, guano and 25 whalers. On December 1, 1864 the ship fired salutes to President Lincoln. It also had a very bad leak after a storm and discovered five feet of water in the hold.

metadata.description: Logbook of a whaling voyage to the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. Includes descriptions of whales seen or taken, accidents, illnesses, desertions, punishments, and shipboard medicine. Also contains whale stamps, profile views, accounts, and a crew list. Three men were sick with scurvy on November 17, 1841. The ship landed at Maui and traded oil and flour for goats and pineapples on April 21, 1842. One man cut two of his toes off with a mincing knife on June 20, 1842. First mate Stephen R. Delano was left at Maui due to sickness on 26 August 1842, with the logbook being pooly kept as a result after this date. Whaling grounds include the Coast of Chile, Off Shore, Galapagos, On the Line, Coast of Brazil, and the 36/36 grounds.; Old Dartmouth Historical Society (ODHS 328); Whaling vessel out of Fairhaven, Mass., mastered by Samuel Perry, on voyage 18 December 1840 - 22 April 1843; managing agent, Hiram Henry Stackpole; built in Kennebunk, Maine.

metadata.description: Journal, kept by Andrew J. Wing, comprised of two whaling voyages. First voyage documents the Adeline (Ship) of New Bedford, Mass., mastered by Albert D. Barber, from 19 September 1860 - 7 May 1865 returning from the North Pacific Ocean. The oil, molasses, and various provisions from the Milo were stowed on the Adeline and "so ends the most disagreeable voyage that I ever saw in 26 years of whaling." Second voyage documents the Milo (Ship) of New Bedford, Mass., mastered by Jonathan C. Hawes, from 1 December 1863 - 9 May 1868 to the South Atlantic Ocean, Sandwich Islands, Anadyr Sea, and North Pacific Ocean. Pages 10-68 contain the account of the voyage including a man overboard and lost, accounts of ice in the Arctic Ocean --Description and travel, seeing wolves, and catching walrus. Within this, there are pages missing. Pages 2-5 contain accounts of the ship Kutusoff in 1855-56; pages 138-148 contain records of the bark Addison.

metadata.description: Le 3 août 1492, Christophe Colomb entame son fabuleux voyage. Ce n'est que bien plus tard qu'on se rendra compte qu'il n'a pas eu seulement pour résultat la découverte d'un nouveau continent mais qu'il a aussi marqué la fin d'une période de notre histoire. Une page est tournée. C'est la fin du Moyen Age. L'humanité a remporté une victoire sur les forces obscures de la nature. Les mers et les océans de notre planète apparaissent sur les cartes. La preuve que la terre est ronde est définitivement établie. Le commerce international peut donc se développer. Après 1492, les pays européens vont connaître un nouvel essor économique. Mais la vague de colonisation qui va suivre les découvertes de Colomb aura de nombreux côtés négatifs. L'Européen respecte très peu la culture des peuples qu'il rencontre. Pillages, massacres et dévastations en masse. La découverte des Amériques fut aussi le début d'une période de génocide et de soumission des plus barbares.

Fur trader (Wallace, Dictionary of Canadian biography ). // Bibaud, Michel: 1782-1857. // Huntington, Jedediah Vincent: 1815-1862. // Also published, 2nd edition, New York: Redfield, 1854 (376p.). This is said to have provided the foundation for Washington Irving's Astoria, or, anecdotes of an enterprise beyond the Rocky Mountains . Donnelley & Sons, 1954 (liii, 318, [3]p.), reprinted, New York: Citadel Press, 1968 (liii, 318p.); as Adventure at Astoria, 1810-1814 , translated and edited by Hoyt C. Franchère, Norman: University of Oklahoma Press, 1967 (xxix, 190p.); as Journal of a voyage on the north west coast of North America: During the years 1811, 1812, 1813, and 1814 , translated by Wessie Tipping Lamb, edited by W. Kaye Lamb, Toronto: Champlain Society, 1969 (ix, 330, xixp.). For French version see Peel 81.

metadata.description: Logbook kept by Josiah C. Long comprised of eight whaling voyages. First voyage documents the Foster (Ship) of Nantucket, Mass., mastered by Shubael Chase, from 24 June 1822 - 27 December 1824 to the Pacific Ocean Contains a long description of the Bounty mutiny and people on Pitcairn Island. The crew also witnessed a total solar eclipse on 26 June 1824. Second voyage documents the Foster (Ship) of Nantucket, Mass., mastered by Edy Coffin, from 7 June 1825 - 16 October 1827 to the Brazil banks, South Pacific Ocean and coast of ChileDuring this voyage the ship saw 125 whales and caught 97. During a stop at the Juan Fernández Islands the ship was able to obtain peaches for the ship. There was one death at sea. Third voyage documents the Foster (Ship) of Nantucket, Mass., mastered by Job C. Clark, from 19 April 1828 - 30 June 1829 to western and southern Atlantic Ocean for sperm and right whales [spelled "write"]. Fourth voyage documents the Foster (Ship) of Nantucket, Mass., mastered by Job E. Clark, from 15 November 1829 - 27 January 1833 to the Atlantic Ocean and Pacific Ocean sIn the company of several other vessel at times. Put into port at Rio de Janeiro for repairs. Fifth voyage documents the Foster (Ship) of Nantucket, Mass., mastered by Josiah C. Long, from 27 June 1833 - 16 November 1836 along Brazil and Chile and the South Pacific OceanDuring the voyage they saw 86 whales and caught 52. They spoke the Charles Carroll's captain Owen Chase who was a survivor of the Essex. Sixth voyage documents the Foster (Ship) of Nantucket, Mass., mastered by Josiah C. Long, from 1 September 1837 - 28 April 1841 to waters off Brazil, Chile, Peru and the South Pacific OceanThe ship encountered rough weather and could not reach the Azores. During the voyage nine men contracted smallpox. Seveth voyage documents the Richard Mitchell (Ship) of Nantucket, Mass., mastered by Josiah C. Long, from 14 October 1843 - 30 September 1847 to Brazil, Galapagos Islands, and the South Pacific OceanIncludes comments on the residents of Pitcairn Islands. It took the ship a month to round Cape Horn. Eighth voyage documents the Charles Carroll (Ship : 1832-1853) of Nantucket, Mass., mastered by Josiah C. Long, from 2 December 1848 - 29 December 1852 along the coast of Peru and the South Pacific Ocean. Voyage began by wrecking the rudder on an oil cask. Includes data on all vessels included in journal.

metadata.description: Logbook of a whaling voyage to the Atlantic, Pacific and, Arctic Oceans in addition to the Anadyr and Kamchatka Seas. Includes description of types of whales, seals, and walruses seen or taken, accidents, injuries, several deaths at sea, a fire on a ship, mutinous behavior, interactions with natives, punishments, a rescue at sea, and shipboard medicine. Also contains whale stamps, accounts, provisions used, and inventories of oil and bone. During the voyage the captain often disagreed with his charts. The keeper notes that there were 70-100 ships in the Arctic on 15 November 1852 and 100 ships (30 whalers) at Hong Kong on February 21 1852. The captain suffered an injury on December 24, 1850. While at Nauru [Pleasant Island] on 17 June 1852, the natives took the crew to the kings. The keeper records the death of Captain Joseph Bailey of the ship Champion on February 28, 1852. At one point, the vessel was damage in a gale. In 1852, the forecastle was smoked due to one of the crew dying of smallpox. Whaling grounds include the On the Line, Kamchatka, and the Arctic grounds.; Old Dartmouth Historical Society (ODHS 92); Whaling vessel out of New Bedford, Mass., mastered by Charles Slocum, on voyage 8 October 1850 - 10 May 1853; managing agent, Charles Hitch; built in Nobleboro, Maine.

metadata.description: Journal, keeper unknown, managing agent I. Howland, Jr. & Co., relating to whaling voyage in the South Pacific and Arctic. One line per day recorded August 1850 - December 25. Activities recorded include illnesses and accidents, taking on of recruits, assorted ship repairs, retrieving a cask full of sperm oil, hiring Maoris to hunt for deserters, finding women on the ship and having to chase them off the ship twice, and the keeper's nostalgia for the fourth of July at home.

metadata.description: In 2011, NASAs Aeronautics Research Mission Directorate (ARMD) funded an effort to develop an ablative thermal protection system (TPS) material that would have improved properties when compared to Phenolic Impregnated Carbon Ablator (PICA) and AVCOAT. Their goal was a conformal material, processed with a flexible reinforcement that would result in similar or better thermal characteristics and higher strain-to-failure characteristics that would allow for easier integration on flight aeroshells than then-current rigid ablative TPS materials. In 2012, NASAs Space Technology Mission Directorate (STMD) began funding the maturation of the best formulation of the game changing conformal ablator, C-PICA. Progress has been reported at IPPW over the past three years, describing C-PICA with a density and recession rates similar to PICA, but with a higher strain-to-failure which allows for direct bonding and no gap fillers, and even more important, with thermal characteristics resulting in half the temperature rise of PICA. Overall, C-PICA should be able to replace PICA with a thinner, lighter weight, less complicated design. These characteristics should be particularly attractive for use as backshell TPS on high energy planetary entry vehicles. At the end of this year, the material should be ready for missions to consider including in their design, in fact, NASAs Science Mission Directorate (SMD) is considering incentivizing the use of C-PICA in the next Discovery Proposal call. This year both scale up of the material to large (1-m) sized pieces and the design and build of small probe heatshields for flight tests will be completed. NASA, with an industry partner, will build a 1-m long manufacturing demonstration unit (MDU) with a shape based on a mid LD lifting body. In addition, in an effort to fly as you test and test as you fly, NASA, with a second industry partner, will build a small probe to test in the Interactive Heating Facility (IHF) arc jet and, using nearly the same design, build the aeroshell and TPS, with instrumentation, for a small probe flight test article, due to fly in 2017. At the end of the year, the C-PICA will be at TRL 5+, and with the flight data in 2017, it will be at TRL 9 for missions needs with C-PICA at a small scale (12 diameter). The scale-up and small probe efforts will be de-scribed in this presentation.

metadata.description: Description : Index of the oral history interview of Milos Kovac, aka Shilos Kovac, a well-known member of the Southern European community in Sacramento. The interview took place on November 11, 1983 by Lyn Maners as part of the Sacramento Ethnic Communities Survey Collection. Click here  to stream the audio of this oral history interview.  The Sacramento Ethnic Communities Survey Collection was created in the 1980s as the basis for a major installation at the (then-named) Sacramento History Center. Over thirty-five advisers, researchers, scholars, and planners spent one year gathering data. Analysis of the federal census records revealed over 150 ethnic groups in the Sacramento region. Based on the information in the census records, researchers determined that twenty-two groups maintained an identity over time and shaped the social and cultural history of Sacramento. These are the groups represented in the survey. For each group the survey team wrote a community history, copied photographs that documented the community, and captured oral histories with prominent members. The exhibition lasted nearly a decade at the museum and upon its removal an educational CD ROM was created and distributed to the public to ensure the effort lived on. Plans originally called for the publication of the written manuscript histories and the transcriptions of the oral histories but the funding was never secured. With the help of Center for Sacramento History volunteers, historical societies, and local ethnic community groups, some of the oral history interviews have been transcribed. metadata.description: This paper aims to examine the role of relationships between organizational factors, employee resilience and work outcomes, in order to test the mediatory role of employees in hospitality kitchens in Serbia. The paper represents a quantitative study; the research was conducted through a questionnaire which served as a means for collecting reliable data. The data were obtained from 182 respondents employed in hospitality kitchens in Serbia. The results of this research have shown that resilience has a mediatory role between organizational factors and work outcomes. This paper deals with an important research subject, which is currently not given enough attention, which is indicated by the fact that this type of research has not yet been conducted in hospitality kitchens.

metadata.description: Exercising the child’s right to work requires a good legislative framework for labour relations and a set of conditions prescribed to ensure that the minors work in a way that does not harm their safety, health, physical, mental and moral development and does not interfere with their education. The aim of this paper is to consider both the international and national standards regulating the children’s work and challenges in their application in practice. It also points out the necessary actions aimed at improving the position of the minors in the labour law environment. A special attention is paid to the issues related to the prohibition of discrimination against children in the field of work, the consent for employment including the regulation of the minimum age for employment and protection at work. The paper focuses in particular on the issue of the implementation of labour legislation in practice of Republic of Serbia, especially in the context of the efficiency of control mechanisms and the results of inspections conducted in 2019 by the Labour Inspectorate of the Ministry of Labour, Employment, Veteran and Social Affairs, which revealed a series of violations of the child’s right to work. In this paper, in order to grasp an insight into this issue, there have been used the historical comparative-legal and theoretical-analytical methods. The research findings indicate that the national labour legislation regulating the minors` work is harmonised with the international standards to a significant extent, but there is a room for their improvement. It is also necessary to improve the mechanisms of inspection and the efficiency of the application of legislative provisions in practice.

metadata.description: Integrated subsystem health diagnostics is an area where major improvements have been identified for potential implementation into the design of new reusable launch vehicles (RLVs) in order to reduce life cycle costs, to increase safety margins, and to improve mission reliability. This talk summarizes a joint effort between NASA Ames and industry partners to develop rapid non-contact diagnostic tools for health and performance monitoring of thermal protection systems (TPS) on future RLVs. The specific goals for TPS health monitoring are to increase the speed and reliability of TPS inspections for improved operability at lower cost. The technology being developed includes a 3-D laser scanner for examining the exterior surface of the TPS, and a subsurface microsensor suite for monitoring the health and performance of the TPS. The sensor suite consists of passive overlimit sensors and sensors for continuous parameter monitoring in flight. The sensors are integrated with radio-frequency identification (RFID) microchips to enable wireless communication of-the sensor data to an external reader that may be a hand-held scanner or a large portal. Prototypes of the laser system and both types of subsurface sensors have been developed. The laser scanner was tested on Shuttle Orbiter Columbia and was able to dimension surface chips and holes on a variety of TPS materials. The temperature-overlimit microsensor has a diameter under 0.05 inch (suitable for placement in gaps between ceramic TPS tiles) and can withstand 700 F for 15 minutes.

"For the first time ever, the two people who knew Andy Kaufman best open up about the most enigmatic artist of our generation. Comedian and Taxi star Andy Kaufman, known for his crazy antics on screen and off, was the ultimate prankster, delighting audiences with his Elvis and Mighty Mouse impressions while also antagonizing them with his wrestling and lounge lizard alter ego, Tony Clifton. In 1984, some say he died while others believe he performed the ultimate vanishing act. At last, in Andy Kaufman: The Truth, Finally, Bob Zmuda, Andy's writer and best friend, and Lynn Margulies, the love of Andy's life, reveal all, including surprising secrets that Andy made Lynne and Bob promise never to tell until both of his parents had died. Hilarious and poignant, this book separates fact from fiction, and includes a candid inside take on the Milos Forman film Man on the Moon, which starred Jim Carrey as Andy, Paul Giamatti as Zmuda, Courtney Love as Margulies and Danny DeVito as Andy's manager, George Shapiro. Zmuda and Margulies reveal what was truthful and what wasn't and share their behind-the-scenes Kaufmanesque antics they concocted with actor Jim Carrey, keeping him in character, at times, much to the chagrin of studio chiefs. Andy Kaufman also exposes intrigues of some of the biggest names in Hollywood. Finally, Bob Zmuda shares-in detail-the reasons he believes Andy Kaufman did, in fact, fake his own death, including exactly how he did it and when and where Andy will return. "--

metadata.description: The main assumptions the Copenhagen quantum mechanics has been based on will be summarized and the known (not yet decided) contradiction between Einstein and Bohr will be newly analyzed. The given assumptions have been represented basically by time-dependent Schroedinger equation, to which some further assumptions have been added. Some critical comments have been raised against the given mathematical model structure by Pauli (1933) and by Susskind and Glogover (1964). They may be removed if only the Schroedinger equation is conserved and the additional assumptions are abandoned, as shown recently. It seems to be in contradiction to the numerous declarations that the Copenhagen model has been approved by experimental results. However, in the most of these experiments only the agreement with the mere Schroedinger equation has been tested. All mentioned assumptions have been tested practically only in the EPR experiment (measurement of coincidence light transmission through two polarizers) proposed originally by Einstein (1935). Also these experimental results have been interpreted as supporting the Copenhagen alternative, which has not been, however, true. In fact the microscopic world may be described correspondingly only with the help of the hidden-variable theory that is represented by the Schroedinger equation without mentioned additional assumptions, which has the consequence that the earlier interpretation gap between microscopic and macroscopic worlds has been removed. The only difference concerns the existence of discrete states. The possibilities of the human reason of getting to know the nature will be also shortly discussed in the beginning of this contribution.
metadata.title: Hidden-variable theory versus Copenhagen quantum mechanics

metadata.description: Crna Gora I Pleme Vasojevići - Uvijek Su Bili Jedno .  KOMUNIN VREMEPLOV  • Uvijek su bili jedno • Komun@ broj 19 • Piše dr  Draško Došljak • Vasojevići su pleme koje je nastanjeno u istočnom dijelu Crne Gore (matica Lijeva Rijeka) i obje strane rijeke Lima sve do rijeke Lješnice. O njihovom imenu i porijeklu u narodnom predanju žive dvije verzije. Prvo predanje govori da su Vasojevići potomci izvjesnog Vasa, rodnika Vukana Nemanjića, koji je rođen u Prizrenu, a bio je vojvoda u vrijeme cara Dušana. Drugo predanje porijeklo Vasojevića vezuje za nekog Vasa, sina nekoga hercegovačkoga kralja, koji se preko Crne Gore doselio iz Hercegovine i nastanio na Nožici u Lijevoj Rijeci. Pavel Apolonovič Rovinski, koji je u Crnoj Gori boravio tridesetak godina, proučavajući njenu prošlost ističe da „Vasovi potomci nijesu znali da objasne odakle i kada je Vaso došao u Crnu Goru“. Prvobitna plemenska teritorija Vasojevića formirana je u Lijevoj Rijeci u periodu od druge polvine XV do sredine XVI vijeka, ujedinjavanjem brastava crnogorskog podneblja, a Vaso je bio, možda, prvi vasojevićki čelnik. Prvi pisani pomen Vasojevića nalazimo 1444. odine. Konstantin Jiriček navodi jedan dokument iz te godine koji se čuva u Dubrovačkom arhivu. U tom dokumentu stoji da se izvjesni Brajan Prodanić žali dubrovačkom sudu kako mu je šesdeset gorštaka: Pipera, Bjelopavlića i Vasojevića napalo trgovački karavan, ubilo brata i opljačkalo robu. Ako uzmemo činjenicu da je potrebno stotinak godina da se nekoj plemenskoj zajednici i lokalitetu ustali ime, onda se može pretpostaviti da se predak Vasojevića ovdje doselio polovinom 14. vijeka. U istoriji Crne Gore ističe se više ličnosti iz Vasojevića koji su odigrali važnu ulogu u njenim ratnim i mirnodopskim vremenima. Veliku podršku Petar II Petrović Njegoš je imao od igumana Đurđevih stupova Mojsija Zečevića. „Kao čovjek od posebnog povjerenja, čije je pregovaračke sposobnosti izuzetno cijenio, Njegoš je igumanu Zečeviću davao delikatne političke zadatke. To se vidi iz jednog Njegoševog pisma bosanskom paši, u kojem poručuje: Sve što ti iguman reče, to ti mi zborimo, i sve što s njim uglaviš, znadi dobro da s nama glaviš.... Upravo zahvaljujući igumanu Zečeviću, ali i drugim uglednim prvacima, Crna Gora je snažila svoj uticaj u Vasojevićima i čitavom Polimlju. Veliki broj Vasojevićkih glavara održavao je bliske veze sa slobodnom Crnom Gorom, tako da je i prije formalnog prisajedinjenja Vasojevića Crnoj Gori ovdje funkcionisala crnogorska vlast“. Jedna od značajnih ličnosti koje su Vasojevići u 19. vijeku dali Crnoj Gori, svakako, je i Miljan Vukov Vešović, koga je „Njegoš pobratimio sa svojim nasljednikom Knjazom Danilom, želeći da i time učvrsti vezu između Vasojevića i Crne Gore. On je vojvodsko zvanje dobio sa Cetinja. Kako bilježi njegov sin vojvoda Gavro Vuković, kad je proglasio prisajedinjenje Vasojevića Crnoj Gori, i to saopštio Knjazu Danilu, on ga je, plašeći se da Vasojevići zbog toga ne postradaju, oslobodio bilo kakvih obaveza. Ali, Vojvoda Miljan Vukov bio je odlučan: „Ostajem s tobom i Crnom Gorom“, odgovorio je Knjazu Danilu. Godina 1853. je veliki datum za istoriju Vasojevića. To je , dakle, godina kada je „još jedna Crna Gora prislonjena Crnoj Gori“. Važnu ulogu u ovome odigrao je, upravo, Miljan Vukov. O njemu će pisar vojvode Peka Pavlovića, Jovan Nikolić zapisati: „Znam ga kao velikog rodoljuba. On ljubi domovinu, iako ima nekijeh koji ga krive da drži nekakve odnošaje sa Srbijancima. Nije tu štete nikakve, no neka drži, i tamo su naša braća. A on neće ništa učiniti što bi naudilo ugledu i časti domovine, a zbog takvijeh veza nikome štete neće biti. To govore za njega oni kojima sve smeta što čini i što radi njegovo pleme, eto skoro od Morače do Lima. Baga mi, niko nije toliko zadužio Crnu Goru, poslije kuće Petrovića, koliko on“. Serdar Jole Piletić je o Miljanu Vukovu Vešoviću istakao: „Miljan je ima mač u ustima a ne jezik ! Govorio je odrešito ko da mačem sijeva“ Pri jednom susretu na Cetinju Jole Miljanu reče: „ Ti postade knjaz Nahije, Miljane. Pa bez kapetana i perjanika nikud!“ Miljan Vukov mu odgovori: „Lako je vana ovamo. Sve imate gotovo, stvorili ste prije, a mi stvaramo sve iz početka, ka čovjek kad ozida kuću i počne da se okućava i sređuje“. Prisajedinjenje Vasojevića Crnoj Gori, bio je jedan od najvažnijih događaja u crnogorskoj istoriji. Zadatak vojvode Miljana Vukova i vasojevićkih glavara je bio da se odmah uspostavi vlast kakvu je imala Crna Gora u njenim starim granicama. Zanimljiv je jedan događaj iz 1861. godine koji je vezan za Vasojeviće i Miljana Vukova, a koji ovom prilikov valja apostrofirati. Naime, vojvoda Miljan je te godine dobio nalog od knjaza Nikole da spremi odred od 300 boraca koji treba da preko turske teritorije dođe na granicu Srbije milom ili silom. Vojvoda Miljan je kraj manastira Đurđevi stupovi okupio je odred hrabrih Vasojevića i komandu,za ovaj zadatak, povjerio je Šuju Šćepanovom Dragoviću i „otposla ih kroz turske zemlje – za Srbiju... Na srbijansku granicu stigli su sa devet ranjenih, dva poginula, ali i sa trofejima: 21 posječena turska glava. Tu ih je čekalo iznenađenje. Vlada Mihaila Obrenovića, poslala im je u susret generala Ranka limpića, da ih razoruža! Vasojevići se ne htješe raspasti. Kad je ovaj pohod poslije iplomatskih peripetija bio završen – knjaz Nikola podiže na Cetinju pomenik u znak sjećanja a izdajstvo Srbije“. Spomenik je podignut 1861. godine na platou pored Vlaške crkve. Spomenik je bio od lesanog kamena, kupastog oblika, visine oko 3 metra, sa kamenim krstom na vrhu. Uklonjen je krajem 19. vijeka uz obrazloženje da se proširuje Bajova ulica. Nakon proširenja ulice, spomenik nije vraćen! Nema ga ni danas. Na spomeniku su bila uklesana sljedeća imena: Ivo Jovov Ivanović, Novo Boćinin Ayić, Mirko Paunov Vešović – Popović, Mirko Lukin Vešović – Popović, Mitar Radosavov Milošević, Tomaš Radulov Milošević, Aleksa Milošev Drekalović, Risto Savov Vešović – Popović, Radonja Milićev Vešović – Popović, Mihailo Božinin Zečević,Nikola Jovanov Lašić – Dabetić, Miloš Mitrov Lašić – Dabetić, Vukota Radonjin Ayić, Milum Novov Vešović – Popović, Risto Popov Popović, Radoje Đurov Ljubić-Boričić, Tomica Vukov Milikić, Jovan Milošev Zečević, Mitar Radojev Kruščić, Jovan Mitrov Ayić, Veliša Milutinov Ayić, Đoko Petrov Đukić, Veljo Ćetkov (Mirkov) Ayić, Mihailo Jankov Boričić i Đoko Tomov Boričić. Na ovom spomeniku su bila i sljedeća imena poginulih iz Lijeve Rijeke: Mihailo Petrov Dabetic, Ilija Jovanov Orović, Majo Mišov Đeković – Milošević, Jovan Radovanov Vešović –Popović. Važna ličnost za Crnu Goru iz Vasojevića je, nesumnjivo, Gavro Vuković, prvi diplomirani pravnik u Crnoj Gori i ministar spoljnih djela. Njegovi memoari (tri toma) su svjedočanstvo o Crnoj Gori u jednom burnom vremenu. Odnos Vasojevića prema Crnoj Gori iskazivali su vasojevićki književnici, slikari, umjetnici, naučnici, političari... Vasojevići i oni koji su živjeli i stvarali na ovom prostoru. Književnik Dušan Kostić i stihom poručuje: „Ako je ljubim, goru moju čarnu, možda znam zašto je ljubim.“ A veliki Radovan Zogović, beranski gimnazijalac u pjesmi „Internacija Crne Gore“, veli: „Kreći! Crnogorci su krivi jer misle da je Crna Gora njihova Crna Gora.“ Poezija, često, rječitije i odgovornije zbori o stvarnosti. A, Vasojevići i Crna Gora su stvarnost. Ne kreći!!! Rečeno je i prije deset godina: DA – Crnoj Gori. Prisajedinjenjem Vasojevića Crnoj Gori , kako reče vojvoda Marko Miljanov Popović, vojvoda Miljan Vukov Vešović je „Crnoj Gori prislonio još jednu Crnu Goru“. Da je vječna Crna Gora!

metadata.description: To market products with geographical indications in the best possible way, it is necessary to examine the attitudes and habits of consumers. The subject of this paper is a survey on habits and attitudes of consumers about products with GI in Serbia. The aim of this paper is to examine the level of familiarity, attitudes, and habits of consumers, as well as to determine the knowledge and interest in these products. Citizens of Serbia participated in the research (n = 399). The methodology is based on a questionnaire that obtained the data that were processed via t-test statistical methods for independent samples, one-factor analysis of variance, the χ² test, and Pearson’s correlation coefficient. Based on the conducted research, it can be stated that about 70% of respondents are willing to pay a higher price for these products.

metadata.description: We analyze the duration of the unbiased Avoider-Enforcer game for three basic positional games. All the games are played on the edges of the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and Avoider's goal is to keep his graph outerplanar, diamond-free and $k$-degenerate, respectively. It is clear that all three games are Enforcer's wins, and our main interest lies in determining the largest number of moves Avoider can play before losing. Extremal graph theory offers a general upper bound for the number of Avoider's moves. As it turns out, for all three games we manage to obtain a lower bound that is just an additive constant away from that upper bound. In particular, we exhibit a strategy for Avoider to keep his graph outerplanar for at least $2n-8$ moves, being just 6 short of the maximum possible. A diamond-free graph can have at most $d(n)=\lceil\frac{3n-5}{2}\rceil$ edges, and we prove that Avoider can play for at least $d(n)-3$ moves. Finally, if $k$ is small compared to $n$, we show that Avoider can keep his graph $k$-degenerate for as many as $e(n)$ moves, where $e(n)$ is the maximum number of edges a $k$-degenerate graph can have.
metadata.title: On winning fast in Avoider-Enforcer games

metadata.description: We develop a novel probabilistic approach for multi-label classification that is based on the mixtures-of-experts architecture combined with recently introduced conditional tree-structured Bayesian networks. Our approach captures different input-output relations from multi-label data using the efficient tree-structured classifiers, while the mixtures-of-experts architecture aims to compensate for the tree-structured restrictions and build a more accurate model. We develop and present algorithms for learning the model from data and for performing multi-label predictions on future data instances. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves highly competitive results and outperforms the existing state-of-the-art multi-label classification methods.

metadata.description: We use cosmological simulations to assess how the explosion of the first stars in supernovae (SNe) influences early cosmic history. Specifically, we investigate the impact by SNe on the host systems for Population~III (Pop~III) star formation and explore its dependence on halo environment and Pop~III progenitor mass. We then trace the evolution of the enriched gas until conditions are met to trigger second-generation star formation. To this extent, we quantify the recovery timescale, which measures the time delay between a Pop~III SN explosion and the appearance of cold, dense gas, out of which second-generation stars can form. We find that this timescale is highly sensitive to the Pop~III progenitor mass, and less so to the halo environment. For more massive progenitors, including those exploding in pair instability SNe, second-generation star formation is delayed significantly, for up to a Hubble time. The dependence of the recovery time on the mass of the SN progenitor is mainly due to the ionizing impact of the progenitor star. Photoionization heating increases the gas pressure and initiates a hydrodynamical response that reduces the central gas density, an effect that is stronger in more massive. The gas around lower mass Pop~III stars remains denser and hence the SN remnants cool more rapidly, facilitating the subsequent re-condensation of the gas and formation of a second generation of stars. In most cases, the second-generation stars are already metal-enriched to ~2-5 X 10^{-4}\zsun, thus belonging to Population~II. The recovery timescale is a key quantity governing the nature of the first galaxies, able to host low-mass, long-lived stellar systems. These in turn are the target of future deep-field campaigns with the James Webb Space Telescope.

metadata.description: We study the discrete massless Gaussian Free Field on $\Z^d$, $d\geq2$, in the presence of a disordered square-well potential supported on a finite strip around zero. The disorder is introduced by reward/penalty interaction coefficients, which are given by i.i.d. random variables. Under minimal assumptions on the law of the environment, we prove that the quenched free energy associated to this model exists in $\R^+$, is deterministic, and strictly smaller than the annealed free energy whenever the latter is strictly positive.
metadata.title: A note on the discrete Gaussian Free Field with disordered pinning on Z^d, d\geq 2

metadata.description: The ACIS instrument on board the Chandra X-ray Observatory has been used to carry out the first systematic study of low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs) in M87. We identify 174 X-ray point-sources, of which ~150 are likely LMXBs. This LMXB catalog is combined with deep F475W and F850LP images taken with ACS on HST to examine the connection between LMXBs and globular clusters in M87. Of the 1688 globular clusters in our catalog, f_X = 3.6 +- 0.5% contain a LMXB and we find that the metal-rich clusters are 3 +- 1 times more likely to harbor a LMXB than their metal-poor counterparts. In agreement with previous findings for other galaxies, we find that brighter, more metal-rich clusters are more likely to contain a LMXB. For the first time, however, we are able to demonstrate that the probability, p_X, that a given cluster will contain a LMXB depends sensitively on the dynamical properties of the host cluster. Specifically, we use the HST images to measure the half-light radius, concentration index and central density, \rho_0, for each globular, and define a parameter, \Gamma, which is related to the tidal capture and binary-neutron star exchange rate. Our preferred form for p_X is then p_X \propto \Gamma \rho_0^{-0.42\pm0.11} (Z/Z_{\odot})^{0.33\pm0.1}. We argue that if the form of p_X is determined by dynamical processes, then the observed metallicity dependence is a consequence of an increased number of neutron stars per unit mass in metal-rich globular clusters. Finally, we find no compelling evidence for a break in the luminosity distribution of resolved X-ray point sources. Instead, the LMXB luminosity function is well described by a power law with an upper cutoff at L_X ~ 10^39 erg/s. (abridged)
metadata.title: The ACS Virgo Cluster Survey III. Chandra and HST Observations of Low-Mass X-Ray Binaries and Globular Clusters in M87

metadata.description: The article [Bolthausen et al., 2000] provides a proof of the absence of a wetting transition for the discrete Gaussian free field conditioned to stay positive, and undergoing a weak delta-pinning at height 0. The proof is generalized to the case of a square pinning-potential replacing the delta-pinning, but it relies on a lower bound on the probability for the field to stay above the support of the potential, the proof of which appears to be incorrect. We provide a modified proof of the absence of a wetting transition in the square-potential case, which does not require the aforementioned lower bound. An alternative approach is given in a recent paper by Giacomin and Lacoin.

metadata.description: Based on the review of previous research procedures, can be seen that entrepreneurial leadership represents a complementary aspect of leadership and entrepreneurship, and as such constitutes one of the main factors in the development of small and medium-sized enterprises. In order to connect leadership and entrepreneurship more closely, a comprehensive review of the relevant literature on entrepreneurial leadership, classified through the periods in which it was defined, will be carried out. Through an in-depth perspective, models of leadership evolution through the aspect of entrepreneurship with clear practical implications will be presented. This type of analysis will create a new framework for the development of key competencies that surround entrepreneurial leadership and, on whose influence, organizational growth and development directly depends. This set of competencies is especially important, due to the circumstances that arose after the COVID-19 pandemic, and this means finding a leadership model that will enable organizations to absorb the negative effects of business in the macro environment and lead in the direction of optimal market sustainability. Also, by expanding existing theoretical knowledge about leadership and entrepreneurship, authors strive to provide a new perspective on modern management in turbulent times.

metadata.description: TRADUCCIÓN, INTRODUCCIÓN Y NOTAS DE ROBERTO TORRETTI Cristóbal Joannon, editor de esta serie, me propuso publicar en edición bilingüe un texto clásico de mi elección. Acepté con gusto y elegí el diálogo entre atenienses y melios con que Tucídides cierra el libro quinto de su Historia de la Guerra de los Peloponesios y los Atenienses (capítulos 5.84 a 5.116). En ese diálogo, los embajadores de Atenas intentan demostrar a las autoridades de Melos que a esta ciudad-estado le conviene someterse de buen grado a la dominación ateniense. Antes de enviar embajadores, Atenas ha invadido la pequeña Melos con más de tres mil soldados, que están listos para atacarla si no acepta la invitación. La argumentación ateniense ilustra admirablemente la idea del estado y de las relaciones entre estados que inspiró a los padres de nuestra patria cuando adoptaron el lema nacional. Por ello considero apropiado que este texto clásico se traduzca y edite justamente en Chile. Espero que su lectura resulte refrescante para quienes sean alérgicos como yo a los alardes de indignación moral que heredamos de los profetas de Israel. "The black man suffering at the hands of whites, the white woman sexually threatened by the black man. Both images have long been burned into the American conscience through popular entertainment, and today they exert a powerful and disturbing influence on American's understanding of race. So argues Linda Williams in this inquisitive book, where she probes the bitterly divisive racial sentiments aroused by such recent events as O.J. Simpson's criminal trial. Williams, the author of Hard Core, explores how these images took root, beginning with melodramatic theater, where suffering characters acquire virtue through victimization."--Jacket

metadata.creator: Thomas J. Bryan, Claude/Anthropic
metadata.description: Patterns of Power: The Same Menu at Every Scale is a pivotal framework paper that bridges the series' theories on diffuse societies and surplus-driven elite expansion, shifting the analytical lens to encounters between concentrated states . When the easy frontiers of diffuse, headless societies close, expanding hierarchies inevitably clash with other centralized systems . At this boundary, the paper argues, inter-state war is revealed to be nothing more than warlordism in robes —two apex predators competing for the same administrative annuity, with their justifying domestic stories stripped away in the raw transaction of force . To illustrate this naked exercise of power, the paper cites the Athenian subjugation of Melos in 416 BC, where the Athenians explicitly refused moral pretenses, declaring that "the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must" . The paper's core contribution is the assertion that the victor's menu is scale-invariant . Whether a warlord conquers a village or an emperor subdues a rival nation, they face the identical accountant's problem—converting immediate force into a durable, low-cost revenue stream—and must choose from the same five options : Plunder and withdraw: Cheap up front, but yields only a one-time, non-durable extraction . Decapitate and install: Placing a puppet in a forged, foreign-supported chair that remains brittle and expensive to hold . Assume the chair: Inserting oneself at the top of an intact, pre-existing administrative apparatus—the cheapest durable option, but only available if a seizable apex exists . Force your belief: A slow, expensive gamble to re-educate and convert the population so they eventually police themselves . Blend the elites: Sharing the annuity by co-opting the defeated elite, converting a potential source of rebellion into a partner with a stake in the system . Ultimately, the paper concludes that the availability of these choices is determined by a single, scale-invariant fork: whether the defeated order possessed a seizable apex . If it did, the conqueror can assume the chair and rule cheaply ; if it did not, the conqueror is forced into expensive, long-term state-building . Over generations, any successful build "cools" into the naturalized furniture of reality, setting the stage for the next turn of the historical cycle .

"Made in Asia/America explores the key role video games play within the race-makings of Asia/America. Each of its fourteen critical essays on games, ranging from Death Stranding to Animal Crossing, and five roundtables with twenty Asian/American game makers, examine the historical entanglements of games, Asia, and America, and reveal the ways games offer new modes of imagining imperial violence, racial difference, and coalition. Shifting away from Eurocentric, white, masculinist takes on gaming, the contributors focus on minority and queer experiences, practices, and innovative scholarly methods, to better account for the imperial circulation of games. Encouraging ambiguous and contextual ways of understanding games, the editors offer an "interactive" editorial method, a genre-expanding approach that encourages hybrid works of auto-theory, queer of color theory, and conversation among game makers and scholars to generate divergent meanings of games, play, and "Asian America."; Contributors. Matthew Seiji Burns, Edmond Y. Chang, Naomi Clark, Miyoko Conley, Toby Đõ̂, Anthony Dominguez, Tara Fickle, Sarah Christina Ganzon, Yuxin Gao, Domini Gee, Melos Han-Tani, Huan He, Matthew Jungsuk Howard, Rachael Hutchinson, Paraluman (Luna) Javier, Sisi Jiang, Marina Ayano Kittaka, Minh Le, Haneul Lee, Rachel Li, Christian Kealoha Miller, Patrick Miller, Keita C. "In the 27th century, humanity's greatest technological achievement is the massive, star-powered Temporal Displacement Ring: a portal to the past. Professor Robert Cragg, reeling from his own personal losses, volunteers to be the first-ever time-traveling historian, fleeing into the shadow of the Roman Empire. Instead of dry, dusty bygones, he encounters real people. Commoners and nobility, sailors and businessmen, zealots and legionaries, druids, gladiators and philosophers all cross his path. The past, he finds, is not dead and gone, but very much alive ... alive with wonder, fear, and, perhaps, love"--Back cover

description: Polismannen Nolan Dahl går in på ett kafé, stoppar pistolen i munnen och trycker av. Hans syster Helena chockas svårt och blir remitterad till psykolog Alex Delaware, som försöker få ihop en rättvisande bild av Nolan och ett svar på frågan varför han sköt sig. Strax därefter hittas två handikappade barn mördade med kort mellanrum. Kommissarie Milo Sturgis tar sin vän Alex Delaware till hjälp i utredningen och snart står det klart att någon dödar utifrån egna elitistiska värderingar - tar liv som inte är värda att leva. Men vem är den skoningslöse mördaren? Och hur hör allting ihop med Nolan Dahls självmord? En andlöst spännande och välskriven thriller där till synes separata tragedier vävs samman på ett skarpsinnigt sätt. Jonathan Kellerman har välförtjänt kallats "mästaren av psykologiska thrillers" och jämförts med storheter som Harlan Coben och David Baldacci. Hans böcker om radarparet Alex Delaware och Milo Sturgis har legat etta på topplistor runt om i världen. [Elib]

metadata.description: From the Publisher: From Donna VanLiere-the author of the beloved Christmas Hope series-comes a moving novel of faith, family, and destiny. Jane Gable thinks 1947 will be like every other year in Morgan Hill, Tennessee but it's the year everything changes. Jane first lays eyes on young Milo Turner the day that her abusive, alcoholic father is buried in the Morgan Hill cemetery. The Turners are the first black family ever to move into the area, and while their presence challenges the comfort of many in the small, tight-knit community, Jane and her brother, John, have found new friends. Then tragedy strikes the Turner household, and the Gable family is asked to make a decision that could rip their world apart. One path might open up a whole new world and bring them closer than ever. Or it might bring them nothing but trouble and heartache. On their journey, Jane discovers that angels are all around us, every day, in the most extraordinary-and ordinary-ways. The Angels of Morgan Hill is filled with unforgettable characters who show us the ways and means of the heart and prove that even in the darkest hours, we are never truly alone

"FEVERISH IN PACE AND RICH IN CHARACTERS ... THIS IS A CHILLING AND IRRESISTIBLE THRILLER."--"People" The daughter of a diplomat disappears on a school field trip- lured into the Santa Monica mountains and killed in cold blood. Her father denies the possibility of a political motive. There are no signs of struggle, no evidence of sexual assault, leaving psychologist Alex Delaware and his friend LAPD homicide detective Milo Sturgis to pose the disturbing question: "Why"? Working together with Daniel Sharavi, a brilliant Israeli police inspector, Delaware and Sturgis soon find themselves ensnared in one of the darkest, most menacing cases of their careers. And when death strikes again, it is Alex who must go undercover, alone, to expose an unthinkable conspiracy of self-righteous brutality and total contempt for human life

metadata.description: The initiation of a carcinogenic insult appears to be optimally effective when the cells are insulted in early S phase of the cell cycle. The transformed phenotype has sarcoma associated determinants that are similar to the ectopic determinants found on human sarcoma-tumor tissue. Both these cell types, i.e. chemically transformed human fibroblasts and sarcoma tumor cells, exhibit cellular invasiveness, neoplastic potential and finite but extended lifespan in vitro. Using selection pressures for culturing of human normal cells in culture followed by insulting the DNA we can isolate cells from the transformed phenotype, from cells that will respond to the insult as a toxic insult. The carcinogen-specific DNA adducts formed under these conditions are qualitatively and quantitatively similar.

metadata.description: Examination of the carcinogenic activity of selected hydrazine, polynuclear hydrocarbons and/or napthylamines on human cells was evaluated on human foreskin cell populations in vitro. We also evaluated the interaction of these compounds with feline oncornaviruses (ST-FeSV). To date we understand how this system can be used to evaluate the carcinogenic activity of the above suspected carcinogens. We have listed the chemicals evaluated in this system for their carcinogenic activity. Table 4 presents characteristics of the transformed cells in early, transitional and late stages of the carcinogenic process. The contents to Table 2 Segment 2 summarizes the comparative aspects of the carcinogenic activity and cocarcinogenic activity of the chemicals. In Table 2 Segment 2 it was found that RDDP activity was absent in the carcinogen transformed cells. We can conclude from these data that the induction of the carcinogenic process is not a consequence of indogenous oncornavirus activation. These data presented to date illustrate that human cells can be used to evaluate carcinogens and cocarcinogens on human cells.

metadata.description: Richard Pococke (1704-1765) came from a prominent family. He studied at Cambridge, followed a career in the church and became a prelate. Pococke travelled in Europe (France, Italy, Germany, Austria, Poland, Hungary) together with his cousin from 1733 to 1736. In 1737, he set out on a tour of the East which lasted three years; starting from Egypt, he visited the Holy Land, Cyprus, Crete, the Aegean islands, Asia Minor and modern-day Continental and Northern Greece, the last two being territories hardly trodden by travellers at that time. Pococke travelled in Ireland in the years 1747-1760. From 1765 onwards he made various journeys in Britain as a bishop. ( Ioli Vingopoulou,  Aikaterini Laskaridis Foundation)

description: xiii, 226 pages ; 21 cm

Patrick Hunt brings his top-ten list of ancient archaeological discoveries to life in this concise and captivating book. The Rosetta Stone, Troy, Nineveh's Assyrian Library, King Tut's Tomb, Machu Picchu, Pompeii, the Dead Sea Scrolls, Thera, Olduvai Gorge, and the Tomb of 10,000 Warriors - Hunt reveals the fascinating stories of these amazing discoveries and explains the ways in which they add to our knowledge of human history and permanently altered our worldview. Part travel guide to the wonders of the world and part primer on ancient world history, Ten Discoveries That Rewrote History captures the awe and excitement of finding a lost window into ancient civilization
"A Plume book."
